---
title: "Getting started"
description: "Open Scratch and calculate your first total."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/getting-started
---

# Getting started

**Scratch is a floating spreadsheet for macOS. Its menu bar icon and global shortcut bring up the same workbook from any app.**

## Open Scratch

Scratch is in local preview. If you have a copy of the source, run `make run` from its folder. The build needs macOS 14 or later and Swift 6.

Click Scratch’s menu bar icon or press ⌥ Space. Press Escape on the grid to dismiss it. Open it again to resume at the same selection. The pin beside Notes keeps the grid visible when you switch apps.

On an empty sheet, look at the lower left for a first-run hint. Start typing to edit the selected cell. The hints for typing, opening the command palette and hiding Scratch each retire after you use the action.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/empty-sheet-hint-light.webp" alt="A new sheet with A1 selected and a Type to start hint at the lower left." width="547" height="337" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/empty-sheet-hint-dark.webp" alt="A new sheet with A1 selected and a Type to start hint at the lower left." width="547" height="337" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Add five numbers

1. Type a number and press Return. Repeat for five consecutive rows in column A.
2. In A6, type `=su` and press Tab to complete `=SUM(`.
3. Press Shift+Up five times to select A1:A5. Press Return to show the total.
4. Change one of the inputs. The total updates automatically.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<video class="scratch-light" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Select five values, enter SUM in A6 and extend the reference to A1:A5 with Shift and Up." poster="/docs/first-total-light.webp" width="1080" height="700">
<source src="/docs/first-total-demo-light.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<img class="scratch-light scratch-poster" src="/docs/first-total-light.webp" alt="Select five values, enter SUM in A6 and extend the reference to A1:A5 with Shift and Up." width="1080" height="700" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<video class="scratch-dark" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Select five values, enter SUM in A6 and extend the reference to A1:A5 with Shift and Up." poster="/docs/first-total-dark.webp" width="1080" height="700">
<source src="/docs/first-total-demo-dark.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<img class="scratch-dark scratch-poster" src="/docs/first-total-dark.webp" alt="Select five values, enter SUM in A6 and extend the reference to A1:A5 with Shift and Up." width="1080" height="700" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

Use ⇧⌘N to create a sheet and ⌘K to [find a sheet by name](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/shortcuts.md#switch-sheets). Each sheet has its own grid, notes and column widths. Scratch autosaves the workbook locally. **Delete Current Sheet** removes a sheet from the workbook view. **Restore Deleted Sheet** recovers it, including its notes, after a restart.

## Change the shortcuts

Click **⋯ → Keyboard Shortcuts** to change the shortcuts for opening Scratch, capturing the clipboard, Notes or the command palette. **Capture Clipboard in New Sheet** is also available from the ⋯ menu and the command palette. [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/shortcuts.md).

## Choose the look and motion

Open **⋯** and choose **Animation Style**. **Natural** is the default. **Snappy** shortens transitions, and **Off** turns them off. The docked Notes pane reveals from its divider. Nearby cell jumps scroll into view, and distant ones land with a short fade. macOS Reduce Motion skips the movement. Scratch uses a solid window background when Reduce Transparency is on.

Turn on **Follow System Accent** in the same menu to use the accent from macOS. Scratch uses a coral accent by default. Formula references have their own colours so you can match the formula to the cells in the grid.


---
title: "Grid and shortcuts"
description: "Move, edit, format and calculate from the keyboard."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid
---

# Grid and shortcuts

**Type on the grid to edit the selected cell. Return commits and moves down. Tab commits and moves right, or accepts the visible formula suggestion first.**

## Grid toolbar

Use the labeled controls just above the formula bar. **Freeze** keeps headings in view, **Sort** and **Filter** use the selected column, **Export** offers file formats for the current selection or workbook, and **Tables** creates or finds a named table. The freeze and filter buttons highlight while those features are active. Filtered row numbers also take the accent colour. Hover a column letter and click its chevron to open the same controls at that column.

The footer shows a selection’s sum, average and count when they’re available. A uniform number, currency or percent format carries through to the totals. Copying a result keeps its full precision.

## Move and select

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrows | Move between cells |
| Shift+Arrows | Extend or shrink the selection |
| ⌘+Arrows | Move to the next edge of populated data |
| ⇧Space, ⌃Space | Select the current row or column |
| ⌘A | Select the data block. Press again for the populated bounds. |
| F2, Escape | Edit the cell in place, or cancel the edit |
| Delete | Clear the selected cells |
| ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z | Undo or redo an edit |

Shift+Tab and Shift+Return reverse direction. Tab wraps within a selected block. After tabbing across a row, Return moves to the next row at the column where you started.

Drag from one cell to another to select a range. Hold Shift when you start the drag to extend the current selection from its original cell. Hold the pointer at a grid edge to keep scrolling and selecting. Move back inside the grid to pause scrolling, or release to finish.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/grid-selection-light.webp" alt="The Weekend budget range A1:C5 is selected, with its dimensions beside the drag endpoint." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/grid-selection-dark.webp" alt="The Weekend budget range A1:C5 is selected, with its dimensions beside the drag endpoint." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

While dragging, Scratch shows the selection’s rows × columns. The active cell stands out inside the selected block. Drag the border of a populated selection to move its cells, or hold Option to copy them. The destination shows **Move** or **Copy** and previews the contents. A copy shifts relative references, and a move keeps formula addresses as written. Cell annotations and links stay at their existing addresses. Occupied destinations are protected, and Escape cancels the drag.

Press ⌘F to search displayed values, formulas or notes. Return goes to a match. Escape returns to the pane where you opened Find. Find shows the first 80 matches.

After opening a match, press ⌘F then Return, or choose **Back to Find Origin** in the command palette. Scratch restores your grid selection and scroll position, or your cursor and selection in Notes if you started there. The return position lasts until you use it, open another match or leave the sheet.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/grid-find-origin-light.webp" alt="Find shows Back to Find Origin with the previous range, A1:A5." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/grid-find-origin-dark.webp" alt="Find shows Back to Find Origin with the previous range, A1:A5." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Complete a formula

Type `=su` in a cell to see `SUM(values, …)` and what the function does. Press Tab or click the suggestion to insert `SUM(` and keep typing. Square brackets indicate optional arguments. For example, `XLOOKUP` takes a lookup key, a lookup range, a result range and an optional fallback.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/grid-formula-help-light.webp" alt="The inline SUM suggestion lists its arguments and shows the Tab key." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/grid-formula-help-dark.webp" alt="The inline SUM suggestion lists its arguments and shows the Tab key." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Select separate ranges

Select the first range, then ⌘-click a cell or hold ⌘ while dragging to add another range. From the keyboard, open **Add Range to Selection** in the command palette and enter an address such as `D2:F4`.

Formatting, Delete and **Copy Result** apply across the selection. Overlapping ranges count each cell once. Undo restores the edits and the selection. Press Escape to keep the latest range.

Copying or pasting cell data, filling, replaying commands, viewing selection history and sending selected cells to Obsidian each use one range. Scratch saves the latest range when you leave the sheet or quit.

## Save a named range

Select one rectangle, choose **Name Selected Range**, and enter a name such as `Monthly totals`. Choose **Go to Named Range** and type part of the name to select those cells again. Names are unique within a sheet and move with their cells when you insert or delete rows and columns. If you delete the cells, Undo brings the range back.

Use **Remove Named Range** to remove the name. To use a named range in a formula, see [Work across sheets](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#work-across-sheets).

## Named tables

Click any filled cell in a block of data, then choose **Tables → Create Table from Selection**. Scratch finds the connected block. For an exact range, drag across the header and the rows you want before choosing the command. Check the range and header row in the preview, type a name, and press Return. Press Escape to cancel.

Named tables stay in the grid, with a tinted header and outline so you can see where each one starts and ends. Tables can sit side by side. Click any cell in a table to see its name and range beside **Tables**, or use **Sort**, **Filter**, or **Export** on its cells.

- **Sort** starts with the selected column. Choose a different column if needed, then click **Ascending** or **Descending** to preview the order. Click **Apply Sort** to move the rows. The first row stays as a header. Cells move within the table’s columns. Formula references follow the cells they refer to. Press ⌘Z to undo.
- **Filter** shows matches as you type. Choose counted values or enter part of a displayed value. The panel shows the match count and a **Clear** button. Press Escape to restore the previous filter. Shaded cells mark excluded rows inside the table. Cells beside the table stay visible and row numbers stay in place. The arrow keys skip shaded cells. Each sheet has one active filter. Click the filter count to clear it.
- **Export** saves the table as a CSV named after it. With a filter active, choose **Export Matching Rows as CSV** to include the header and matching data, or choose the table by name to include every row.

Use **Tables** to jump to a table by name. With the cursor inside a table, the picker also offers actions to select it, rename it, or remove its name while keeping its cells. Row and column insertions and deletions update the table’s bounds and clear its active filter.

## Add borders or style a table

Select a rectangle and choose **Format → Cell Borders**. Choose outside, inside, all edges, a bottom rule, or clear borders. The grid previews each choice. Click **Apply** or press Return to save it. Press Escape to cancel or ⌘Z to undo the change.

Use **Format → Format as Table** to preview a bold header, alternating rows, and a rule above the last row. From a single cell, Scratch uses its named table or the connected data block. Drag across the cells first to set the exact range. The last-row option styles the row and keeps its current values and formulas. Use **Tables** to name a range for sorting, filtering, or export.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/grid-format-light.webp" alt="Format as Table offers header, alternating row and last-row rule options before applying." width="496" height="296" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/grid-format-dark.webp" alt="Format as Table offers header, alternating row and last-row rule options before applying." width="496" height="296" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Duplicate a sheet or import a file

Choose **Duplicate Sheet** to create a copy beside the current sheet. The copy includes cells, formulas, formatting, notes, named ranges, and capture evidence. Note links within the sheet point to the copied cells. Links to other sheets keep their destinations. Use **Sync Editable Table with Obsidian** to give the copy its own sync destination.

Choose **Import CSV or TSV** from the sheet menu or command palette, then pick a UTF-8 file. Scratch opens the data in a new sheet named after the file. Quoted fields and embedded line breaks are preserved. Fields beginning with `=` come in as text. Each file can contain up to 2,000 rows and 96 columns and must fit within 10 MB.

After **Delete Current Sheet**, click **Undo** in the footer or press ⌘Z to bring the sheet back. The footer offers Undo for eight seconds and keeps it visible while you hover over it. To bring back a sheet later, open **Restore Deleted Sheet** from the sheet menu or command palette.

## Insert or delete rows and columns

Select a cell or a rectangular range, then open **Rows and Columns** from the sheet menu. You can also find these commands in the command palette.

| Command | What moves |
| --- | --- |
| **Insert Rows Above** | Adds a blank row for each selected row. Existing rows move down. |
| **Insert Columns Before** | Adds a blank column for each selected column. Existing columns move right. |
| **Delete Rows** | Removes the selected rows. Rows below move up. |
| **Delete Columns** | Removes the selected columns. Columns to the right move left. |

Formulas, including references such as `$A$1`, follow the cells that move. Inserting inside a referenced range expands it. Deleting part of a range shrinks it. A formula that loses its source shows `#REF!`. Linked notes, pinned results, and screenshot sources follow their cells too.

Use ⌘Z to undo the edit or ⇧⌘Z to redo it. If an insertion would push data or formatting beyond the last row or column, Scratch leaves the sheet as it was.

## Move, hide or resize rows and columns

Hold Option and drag a row number or column letter. The blue line shows where it will land. To move several rows or columns together, select their headers first with Shift, then Option-drag one of them. Right-click a header for one-step moves, or use **Move Selected Rows Up** and related commands in the palette. Escape cancels and ⌘Z undoes the move. Formula references, linked ranges and formatting travel with the cells. If the move would split a referenced range, select the rest of the range and try again.

Right-click a row number or column letter and choose **Hide Row** or **Hide Column**. Use **Hide Selected Rows** or **Hide Selected Columns** in the command palette for a block. The grid skips hidden cells as you move. Formulas and exports still include their values. Choose **Show All Rows** or **Show All Columns** to reveal them. Hidden headers stay hidden when you reopen the workbook.

Drag the bottom edge of a row header to set its height. Double-click the edge or choose **Fit Row Height** to restore automatic height and let wrapped text size the row again.

## Freeze rows and columns

Select B2, click **Freeze**, and choose **Freeze Above and Left of Selection** to keep row 1 and column A in view as you scroll. **Freeze Top Row** and **Freeze First Column** work independently. Find all three in the sheet menu under **Freeze Panes**, or in the command palette.

Drag the blue grip at the top of a vertical divider or the left end of a horizontal divider. The boundary snaps to a row or column as you drag. Release to save it or press Escape to cancel. **Unfreeze Panes** restores ordinary scrolling. Scratch remembers the boundary per sheet and makes room for scrolling cells when you shrink the window.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/grid-filter-light.webp" alt="A frozen header and first column stay visible while the budget filter shows travel rows." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/grid-filter-dark.webp" alt="A frozen header and first column stay visible while the budget filter shows travel rows." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Sort rows

Click a cell in the column you want to sort by, then click **Sort**. You can also open the column’s chevron and choose **Sort…**. Check the column name and **Rows to move**, then choose **Ascending** or **Descending** to preview the first four results. Click **Apply Sort** to commit or press Escape to close the preview.

To sort an Amount column while keeping a Total on row 5, enter `2:4` in **Rows to move**. You can also select B2:B4 before clicking **Sort**. Scratch moves the other cells in those rows with the amounts. A selection that starts below the first populated row includes its first selected row by default. Use **First row is a header** to keep the first row of the scope in place.

To sort only the columns of a named table, select a cell inside that table. Frozen rows stay put. Numbers and formula results sort by value, text sorts naturally, and blanks go last. Equal values keep their order.

Formulas, annotations, named ranges and live note links follow their cells. If a preview would break up a referenced range, the message names the range and, for a formula on the sheet, its cell. Adjust **Rows to move** to keep the range together. Press ⌘Z to undo a sort or ⇧⌘Z to redo it.

## Filter rows

Select a cell and click **Filter**, or hover a column letter and click its chevron. For a column with a short list of text values, click one or more counted choices. Type a word, number or fragment to search the displayed values. The grid and match count update as you type. Click **Done** or press Return to keep the filter. Press Escape to restore the previous filter and selection. Scratch matches displayed values, including formatted numbers and formula results. Case and accents are ignored. To limit the filter to a row band, select those rows before opening the controls.

The first row stays visible by default. Turn off **First row is a header** to include it when it is unfrozen. Arrow keys and cell entry skip hidden rows. The footer shows how many rows match. Click the filter button in the footer to clear it. Jumping directly to a hidden address also clears the filter.

A sheet-level filter lasts for the session and keeps the underlying rows and addresses intact. Selection operations and calculations still use the selected addresses. Exports and Obsidian sync include all rows within the chosen range. CSV carries the values and current sort order. Freeze panes and Scratch filters are view settings, so set them up in the destination app if you need them there.

## Resize the window

Click **Expand** in the toolbar to fill the usable area of your display. Click **Compact** to return to the previous size. You can also drag the grip at the lower right to set the size yourself or find both commands in the command palette.

When you reopen Scratch, it uses the display under your pointer. Move or resize the compact window there to set that display’s layout. Scratch remembers a separate position and size for each display, including displays you disconnect and reconnect.

In compact mode, opening Notes makes room beside, above or below the grid according to its dock. In expanded mode, you can show or hide Notes without changing the window size. [Drag the Notes divider](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian.md#resize-notes) to give either pane more room.

## Move or detach panes

Show **Notes**, then drag its header grip to the highlighted left, right, top or bottom edge. Drop outside the window to float Notes. Drag the floating grip back to an edge to dock it. You can also drag the grip beside the sheet name to move or detach the grid.

Press Escape during a drag to cancel. Click either grip for its menu. The command palette includes **Dock Notes Left**, **Dock Notes Right**, **Dock Notes Top**, **Dock Notes Bottom**, **Dock Grid Left**, **Dock Grid Right**, **Detach Notes** and **Detach Grid**.

Scratch remembers the Notes size for each edge and the floating window positions across launches. Moving Notes keeps your selected cells and note text in place. Closing the floating Notes window hides it. Click **Notes** to bring it back to its last position.

## Open a sheet in its own window

Drag the sheet name past the edge of the Scratch panel and release. You can also choose **Open Sheet in Window** from the sheet menu or command palette. The larger window keeps its own scroll position and follows edits to that sheet. The floating panel keeps its place. To edit, double-click a cell in the larger window to open it in Scratch.

## Drag out a table or export CSV

Select a single range and drag **Export** from the grid toolbar. Drop it into an app that accepts tab-separated text, or onto the desktop or into Finder to create a CSV. You can also Control-drag inside the selection, or Control-drag the sheet name to export its populated area. The drag label shows the cell range and available formats. Click **Export** to see actions grouped by **Selection**, **Table**, **Sheet** and **Workbook**. The table section appears when the active cell is in a named table.

Choose **Export Selection as CSV** or **Export Sheet as CSV** and pick where to save the file. The larger sheet window also has an **Export CSV** button. The file contains values, including calculated results, and keeps blank cells inside the exported rectangle. If a drop does not land, save the CSV through **Export** and open the file from the destination app.

In Excel, import with **Data → Get Data → From Text/CSV** to read the UTF-8 text correctly. In Google Sheets, use **File → Import → Upload** and choose a comma separator. [Excel import guide](https://support.microsoft.com/en-gb/excel/import-data-from-a-csv-html-or-text-file) · [Google Sheets import guide](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/12236443?hl=en).

## Copy a range for another app

Select one rectangle, then choose **Export → Copy Selection As**, or find **Copy Selection As** in the command palette. Choose a format and paste it into the destination app.

- **Markdown Table** copies up to 100,000 cells with formatted values and calculated results. Paste it into Obsidian or another Markdown editor.
- **Total Sentence** copies the range address and sum, such as `B2:B6 totals $236.80.` Select the input cells you want to add.
- **PNG Image** copies the selected grid cells at 2×, including their formatting. Hidden rows and columns follow the grid view. The image is limited to 4,096 pixels on each side and eight million pixels overall.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/grid-copy-as-light.webp" alt="The Copy A1:C7 palette offers Markdown Table, Total Sentence and PNG Image." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/grid-copy-as-dark.webp" alt="The Copy A1:C7 palette offers Markdown Table, Total Sentence and PNG Image." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Workbooks and sheet archive

Open the sheet menu and choose **Workbooks → New Workbook** or **Open Workbook**. Each `.scratchbook` file keeps its own sheets, formulas and Notes. Scratch saves the current workbook before switching and reopens the last file at launch. Choose **Open Default Workbook** to return to the original workbook.

Use **Archive Current Sheet** to remove it from the sheet picker while keeping it available to formulas and links. The sheet menu lists archived sheets under **Restore Archived Sheet**. Keep at least one sheet visible.

## TSV and Excel files

Use **Export Sheet as TSV** or **Export Selection as TSV** for tab-separated values. Use **Import CSV or TSV** to bring the file back into a new sheet.

Choose **Export Workbook Values to Excel** for an `.xlsx` file containing the sheets and their calculated values. **Import Excel Values** adds the file’s worksheets to the current workbook. Import reads the results Excel saved for formula cells. If a formula has no saved result, recalculate and save it in the spreadsheet app before importing. Scratch workbook files keep editable formulas, formatting and Notes. Excel exchange carries values. A file can include up to 32 sheets, and each sheet must fit within 2,000 rows and 96 columns.

## Preview paste and fill

See how a paste will land before applying it. Drag the fill handle to extend a series of dates. [Capture and paste](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/capture.md).

## Format a range

Hover near a column divider to see its grip and resize cursor. Drag it to resize the column or double-click to fit the contents. **Wrap** grows the row. Press ⌥Return in a wrapped cell to insert a line break.

Choose **Zoom In Sheet**, **Zoom Out Sheet** or **Reset Sheet Zoom** from the command palette. Zoom scales the grid text, rows, columns and grid controls. Scratch remembers the zoom for each sheet.

Use the **Format** menu for currencies, dates, decimals and text. ⌥⌘1 through ⌥⌘6 apply number, currency, percent, date, text and wrap. Use ⌘B or ⌘I to toggle bold or italic. SUM, SUMIF and SUMIFS results start in bold. Toggle bold off for a particular total, or use **Clear Formatting** to return to the default.

Point to a format in the menu or use the arrow keys to preview it on the selected cells. Choose the item to apply it, or press Escape to restore the original appearance. Wrap grows the row when applied. The command palette also opens the menu through **Browse Cell Formats**.

## Calculate and copy

Type `=SUM(` in a cell or in the formula bar, then drag across the cells to enter a range. Hold at the grid edge to reach cells beyond the visible area. Click a single cell to enter its address. Type a comma to pick another range, or press Return to finish the formula.

Click the chevron beside the formula bar or press ⌥⌘E to expand it. Long expressions wrap, and underlined references match the outlines in the grid. The current argument and matching parentheses highlight as you move the caret. Press ⌥⌘E again to collapse the bar and keep editing at the same position. Return commits the edit and Escape cancels it.

Click **ƒx** on a formula cell to see the intermediate results and jump to its references. [Formula Microscope](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/formula-microscope.md).

Open **Command Palette** from the ⋯ menu or press its shortcut (⇧⌘P by default). Type a cell address to jump to it, or try `12 kg to lb` to copy a unit conversion. Currency formatting sets how a value is displayed. It does not fetch exchange rates. [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/shortcuts.md).

### Convert currency

Type `100 AUD to USD` in the command palette. Choose **Fetch ECB Rates** the first time. Scratch shows the converted amount, exchange rate, ECB publication date and the time Scratch fetched it. Choose **Copy** to put the converted number on the clipboard.

Saved rates work offline. After one hour, or after a failed refresh, the palette labels the rate **Saved**. Choose **Refresh ECB Rates** to check for a newer snapshot. A copied number stays fixed when rates change. [ECB reference rates](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html).

Select numbers and press ⌘Return to insert the suggested calculation. Press ⇧⌘C to copy the selected result or sum. **Pin Result** keeps the active cell’s formatted value in a small window above other apps. It updates when the source changes and lasts until Scratch quits.

Drag **Sum** or **Avg** from the footer to a visible empty cell. The outline and label show the destination and formula. Hold Option to drop the current value. Press Escape to cancel or ⌘Z to undo a drop. Clicking a footer result copies it.

From the keyboard, choose **Place Selection Sum in Cell** or **Place Selection Average in Cell** in the command palette. Type an empty destination address, then press Return for a formula or ⌥Return for a fixed value. Choose a cell outside the source range for a live formula.

To extend a value, series or formula, drag the small square at the selection’s bottom-right corner. The grid scrolls if you hold the pointer at the edge. Release to apply the preview, or press Escape to cancel.

Each sheet has 2,000 rows and 96 columns. Undo history lasts for the app session.

Use **Show Selection History** to compare and restore older cell entries and formats after a restart. [Selection History](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/history.md).

Use **Start Recording** to save a sequence of fill, format and clear commands for another range. [Record and Replay](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/replay.md).

## Work across sheets

Use a sheet name and `!` to refer to cells in the same workbook. Put single quotes around names with spaces and double any apostrophe inside the name. For example, `=SUM('Rate Card'!B2:B12)` adds a column from another sheet. References follow a renamed sheet or moved source cells. A circular chain across sheets shows `#CIRC!`.

Use `=SUM(RANGE("Daily total"))` to read a saved range on the current sheet. A name such as `Daily_Total` can also be typed directly as `=SUM(Daily_Total)`.

- `=XLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A2:A50,Prices!B2:B50,"Unknown item")` returns the first exact match. Use a single row or column for each range, with matching sizes. Without a fallback, a missing key shows `#N/A`.
- `=DAYS("2026-11-12","2026-11-01")` returns 11. `DATEVALUE` turns a date written as YYYY-MM-DD into a spreadsheet date number. Apply the Date format to display it as a date.
- `TRIM` removes extra whitespace, `LEN` counts characters, and `LOWER` and `UPPER` change case.

## Check inputs as you edit

Select a range and choose **Check for Numbers**, **Check for Positive Numbers**, or **Check for Duplicates** in the command palette. Apply more than one check to the same range if needed. Blank cells are allowed. Duplicate text matches regardless of case or spaces at the start or end.

An orange marker shows which cells need attention. Select a marked cell to see what to fix beside it. Formula errors such as division by zero are checked automatically. Use **Inspect Formula** to follow a formula error to its source. [Formula Microscope](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/formula-microscope.md).

Use **Manage Input Checks** to remove a rule. Undo restores the rule or a recent edit.


---
title: "Capture and paste"
description: "Bring in clipboard amounts, screenshots and delimited text."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/capture
---

# Capture and paste

**Copy amounts or an image in another app and press ⌥⇧ Space with Scratch running. Scratch opens a new sheet for the capture.**

## Capture amounts

Copy a column of numbers or lines such as `Lunch $12.50`. The new sheet includes a live total. Press ⇧⌘C to copy the total or ⇧⌘J to send the table and notes to Obsidian.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<video class="scratch-light" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Copied café amounts become a Scratch sheet with a calculated total of 29.80." poster="/docs/clipboard-total-light.webp" width="1120" height="780">

</video>
<img class="scratch-light scratch-poster" src="/docs/clipboard-total-light.webp" alt="Copied café amounts become a Scratch sheet with a calculated total of 29.80." width="1120" height="780" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<video class="scratch-dark" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Copied café amounts become a Scratch sheet with a calculated total of 29.80." poster="/docs/clipboard-total-dark.webp" width="1120" height="780">

</video>
<img class="scratch-dark scratch-poster" src="/docs/clipboard-total-dark.webp" alt="Copied café amounts become a Scratch sheet with a calculated total of 29.80." width="1120" height="780" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Read a screenshot

Use ⌃⇧⌘4 to copy a region of the screen. Press ⌥⇧ Space or paste the image with ⌘V in Scratch. Apple Vision reads the screenshot on your Mac. Scratch uses the rightmost amount it recognises in each row. Crop to the amount column if the screenshot has several.

Select a row to inspect its amount beside its source crop in **Review Capture**. Press ⌘U to toggle the pane. Use the left and right chevrons to visit uncertain rows first, then the remaining unchecked rows. Correct any amount in the grid, then click **Mark Correct**. Editing a reviewed row puts it back in review.

Scratch shows the sum of the detail rows and compares it with a recognised printed total. The pane shows the difference when they disagree. Mixed currencies and invalid amounts leave the calculated total unavailable. The source image and review marks are saved with the workbook.

Click **Append**, choose another sheet, then enter the destination columns in item and amount order, with a currency column if the capture has one. For example, enter `B, D` to put items in B and amounts in D. Scratch previews the range below the last populated row in those columns and remembers the mapping for that sheet. Only reviewed detail rows append. The source capture remains available, and ⌘Z undoes the append as one edit.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/receipt-review-light.webp" alt="The Harbour Kitchen receipt sits beside its recognised rows. Scratch compares the printed and calculated totals." width="1520" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/receipt-review-dark.webp" alt="The Harbour Kitchen receipt sits beside its recognised rows. Scratch compares the printed and calculated totals." width="1520" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Choose how to paste

Open **Command Palette** from the ⋯ menu or press its shortcut (⇧⌘P by default). **Paste Values** copies the displayed values into the destination. **Paste Formulas Only** and **Paste Formatting Only** use cells copied in Scratch.

Choose **Preview Paste** to inspect the destination and dimensions in the bar above the grid. The preview leaves the grid in place. Cells that will be replaced are highlighted. Click another cell or use the arrows to move the preview. Choose **Values**, **Formulas**, **Transpose** or **Split**, or press 1 through 4. In Split, choose a separator or press S to cycle through them. Values and Split preserve leading zeros. Return or **Paste** applies the preview and Escape cancels it.

Choose **Preview Paste CSV**, **Preview Paste TSV** or **Preview Paste Semicolon** to inspect a destination before writing. Press T to treat fields as text, D to interpret decimal commas, Return to paste or Escape to cancel. Use text mode for IDs with leading zeros.

## Fill a series

Select the starting cells and drag the small square at the bottom right of the selection. You can also choose a **Preview Fill** command and extend with the arrows before pressing Return. Scratch extends regular number, date and weekday series and shifts relative references when filling formulas.


---
title: "Notes and Obsidian"
description: "Link notes to live cells and send the table and notes to your vault."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian
---

# Notes and Obsidian

**Click Notes to show or hide the current sheet’s notes. The default shortcuts are ⌘J to show or hide Notes and ⌥⌘J to switch focus between Notes and the grid.** [Change the shortcuts](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/shortcuts.md).

## Move Notes

Drag the **Notes** header grip to the left, right, top or bottom edge of the grid window. Drop it outside to put Notes in its own window. Drag the grip back to a highlighted edge to dock. Click the grip for the same options without dragging. The floating editor follows the current sheet and keeps its window position when you hide and show it. [Move or detach panes](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#move-or-detach-panes).

<figure class="scratch-media">
<video class="scratch-light" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Notes moves from the right of the grid to the bottom and back." poster="/docs/notes-live-light.webp" width="1560" height="1060">
<source src="/docs/notes-dock-demo-light.mp4" type="video/mp4">

<video class="scratch-dark" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Notes moves from the right of the grid to the bottom and back." poster="/docs/notes-live-dark.webp" width="1560" height="1060">
<source src="/docs/notes-dock-demo-dark.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<img class="scratch-dark scratch-poster" src="/docs/notes-live-dark.webp" alt="Notes moves from the right of the grid to the bottom and back." width="1560" height="1060" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Resize Notes

Drag the dotted divider to change how much room each pane gets. Double-click to reset it or press Escape during a drag to cancel. The palette offers **Widen Notes**, **Narrow Notes** and **Reset Notes Width** at the sides. At the top or bottom, use **Taller Notes**, **Shorter Notes** and **Reset Notes Height**. Resize floating Notes from its window edge.

Scratch remembers a size for each dock across sheets and launches. When the window is short or narrow, Scratch can temporarily shrink Notes to leave room for the grid. Widen or grow the window to get that space back.

Hide Notes and reopen it on the same sheet to continue from the same selection and reading position. The docked pane reveals from the divider when motion is enabled.

## Format a note

Use the toolbar for headings, bold, italic, lists, checklists and inline code. Click a checkbox to mark it done. ⌘B and ⌘I also work in the notes editor. Scratch shows headings, emphasis, bullets and checkboxes while saving the Markdown source. Move the caret into a list line to edit its markers directly. Use **Show Notes Markdown Source** in the command palette to edit the markers, then **Show Formatted Notes** to switch back.

## Annotate a cell or range

With Notes open, select plain text and Option-drag from inside the selection to a grid cell. Drop inside the current grid selection to annotate that range. Scratch links the selected text to the annotation and confirms the cell address. Click the underlined text in Notes or open the annotation in the grid. Both open the same editor, and edits appear in both places. Use ⌘Z from the grid to undo the link and restore the original note text.

Select a cell or range and choose **Annotate Selection** in the command palette. Start typing as soon as the editor opens. Write up to 2,000 characters and click **Save** or press ⌘Return. A marker appears at the top left of the first cell.

Click the marker or select its cell and click **Annotation** in the grid footer. The **Annotations** button at the bottom of Notes lists the sheet’s annotations. Use **Find Annotations** in the command palette to search by address or text. Annotations are saved with the workbook, and Undo can restore a deleted annotation.

To link an annotation you made before this update, select its matching text in Notes and Option-drag it onto the same cell or range.

## Put a live result in a note

Select a range and Option-drag from inside it into Notes. The insertion marker shows where the live table will land. Add Shift for a live chart or Command for a range link. The label beside the pointer identifies the item before you drop it. Press Escape to cancel or ⌘Z in Notes to undo the insertion.

Select a cell and press ⌥⌘L to insert its live value. Hover over the value to see its sheet, address, displayed result and formula. Click it or press ⌥Return on the selected note link to go to the source. Press ⌃⌘← or choose **Back to Note** to restore the note selection and scroll position.

The command palette also inserts cell and range links, live tables, bar charts, and fixed value snapshots. Pick a source sheet and address to link across sheets. **Find Notes Referencing Selection** finds links in the current sheet’s notes.

A live table previews up to six rows and four columns. Copy or send the note for the full table. A chart accepts one row or up to two columns and previews up to eight positions. Click a bar to open its source cell. Markdown exports include the chart’s source data as a table.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<video class="scratch-light" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Insert the selected budget cells as a live table in Notes, alongside the chart." poster="/docs/notes-live-light.webp" width="1560" height="1060">
<source src="/docs/notes-table-demo-light.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<img class="scratch-light scratch-poster" src="/docs/notes-live-light.webp" alt="Insert the selected budget cells as a live table in Notes, alongside the chart." width="1560" height="1060" loading="lazy" decoding="async">

</figure>

## Repair a note link

Scratch saves a stable reference for each live note link. Renaming a sheet and editing its values preserve the link. If you delete the source sheet, use **Restore Deleted Sheet** to recover it and reconnect the link.

To point a link to a different range on the sheet that contains the note, select the new range and choose **Relink Note Source**. Choose the link to update. Use Undo in Notes to restore its previous target.

## Send the table and notes

Use **Send to ryn** or its shortcut (⇧⌘J by default). Scratch saves a dated copy under `Scratch/Sheets` and appends the table and notes to today’s daily note. Hover over **Send to ryn** to see the vault, delivery mode and included cells before you send. Once Obsidian confirms the delivery, the pane keeps the note name and an **Open** button. Use **Open Saved Sheet in Obsidian** in the Notes menu to open the dated copy. Sending the same sheet again updates its saved copy and leaves one daily note entry when the content is identical.

Choose **Send Selection and Notes** in the palette to append just that range and its notes to the daily note. Choose **Save Sheet to Obsidian** to update just the saved sheet copy.

The handoff uses the Obsidian command line and the configured vault’s Daily Notes settings. The local preview targets the `ryn` vault by default. [Set up the Obsidian CLI](https://obsidian.md/help/cli).

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/notes-delivery-light.webp" alt="The Notes pane shows the Send to ryn button and a receipt with the daily note date." width="1560" height="1060" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/notes-delivery-dark.webp" alt="The Notes pane shows the Send to ryn button and a receipt with the daily note date." width="1560" height="1060" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Save a dated sheet note

Open **Scratch → Sheets** in Obsidian’s file explorer. Each saved sheet has its own named note with the table, notes and save date. Add your own Obsidian content outside Scratch’s generated section so it survives a resave.

The first save creates **Scratch Sheets.base**. Open it from the command palette to find saved sheets by name and date. The table and linked values are snapshots at export time. To refresh them, save the sheet again from Scratch. A saved note uses the sheet’s current sort order and includes rows hidden by a filter.

Use **Copy Markdown** or **Save Markdown File** in the notes menu to take the same notes elsewhere.

## Edit a table in both Scratch and Obsidian

**Yes, Obsidian edits can come back to Scratch.** Edit the note under `Scratch/Editable Tables`, then run **Sync Editable Table with Obsidian** again. Sync runs on demand for the current sheet. Dated copies under `Scratch/Sheets` and entries in your daily note are snapshots.

In Scratch, choose **Sync Editable Table with Obsidian** from the command palette or the Notes menu. The first sync creates a separate note under `Scratch/Editable Tables` in your configured vault. Use **Open Editable Table in Obsidian** to open it again.

Edit the cells in either app, then run **Sync Editable Table with Obsidian** again. Scratch combines edits to different cells. If both apps changed the same cell to different values, Scratch shows the Scratch and Obsidian values side by side. Click an address to jump there, choose a value for each cell, then click **Apply and Sync**. If either value changes before you apply, Scratch shows the updated conflict. Use **Review Obsidian Changes** in the Notes menu or command palette to reopen the review. You can undo a pull in Scratch with ⌘Z.

Use Obsidian’s **Live Preview** to edit the rendered table or **Reading view** to read it. If an older synced note shows Markdown pipes, run **Sync Editable Table with Obsidian** again to refresh its layout in place. In Source mode, Obsidian shows the raw Markdown. Keep the **Editable table** heading and **Open in Scratch** link so Scratch can find the table on the next sync. Install the **Power Tables** community plugin to recalculate compatible formulas in Obsidian. The first row is row 1 in both apps. Keep the table’s row and column count fixed when editing in Obsidian. To extend it, add cells at the right or bottom in Scratch and sync. The editable table can use up to 64 KB of Markdown. Formulas with complex quoting and Power Tables cell styles can stop a sync until you simplify those cells.

The command syncs cell values and formulas on demand. Sort in Scratch and sync to send the new row order. Sync compares cells by address, so sync any Obsidian edits before sorting to reduce conflicts. Use **Save Sheet to Obsidian** or **Send to ryn** to include your Scratch Notes in a dated copy. You can write in the editable note above or below the table.

## Open an export in Scratch

Click **Open in Scratch** in an exported note to return to its source. A sheet export opens the sheet. A selection sent to the daily note opens the selected range. Open the Scratch app once so macOS can recognise its links, and use the workbook that contains the original sheet.

## Search your Obsidian vault

Choose **Search Obsidian Vault** in the command palette, then type at least two characters from a note’s title or text. Results show a matching snippet and the folder, which helps when two notes have the same title. Press Return to open the result in Obsidian or ⌥Return to insert its link into Scratch Notes.

The first search builds a local index in memory. Scratch refreshes it when vault files change. Search covers the first 128 KiB of each Markdown note and shows up to 20 matches. If the vault is unavailable, open it in Obsidian and choose **Retry Vault Lookup**.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/vault-search-light.webp" alt="The Obsidian search shows the Weekend budget note from the demo vault." width="1560" height="1060" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/vault-search-dark.webp" alt="The Obsidian search shows the Weekend budget note from the demo vault." width="1560" height="1060" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>


---
title: "Formula Microscope"
description: "See how a formula evaluates and jump to the cells behind its result."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/formula-microscope
---

# Formula Microscope

**Select a formula cell and click ƒx in the formula bar. You can also choose Inspect Formula from the command palette.**

## Read a calculation

Enter `3` in A1 and `5` in A2. Enter `=SUM(A1:A2)*2` in B1 and inspect it. The microscope shows `16` for the result, `8` for the sum and `2` for the multiplier. Click `A1:A2` to select that range in the grid.

An `IF` formula shows which branch ran. Parts Scratch didn’t evaluate are marked **Not evaluated**. A range shows how many cells it covers. Press Escape to close the microscope and keep the grid open.

Named ranges resolve to the cells they cover. For a cross-sheet reference, the microscope shows the sheet and address in the expression. Jump links are available for references on the current sheet. [Work across sheets](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#work-across-sheets).

## Find a cell behind an error

Set A1 to `0`, B1 to `=12/A1` and C1 to `=B1+1`. Inspect C1 to see the path through B1 to A1. Choose **Go to A1** to jump to the zero divisor. For an error inside the formula itself, such as `=1/0`, the microscope shows the failing step. A formula Scratch cannot parse shows the error above the expression.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/formula-error-light.webp" alt="The Formula Microscope traces a division error to the zero in B2 and offers a jump to that cell." width="840" height="472" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/formula-error-dark.webp" alt="The Formula Microscope traces a division error to the zero in B2 and offers a jump to that cell." width="840" height="472" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Match formula references to the grid

Expand the formula bar to see each reference in a different colour. The same colour outlines its cells in the grid. Repeated references to the same range share a colour.

## See where a pinned result came from

Select a result and choose **Pin Result** in the command palette. Click the chevron beside **Go to Cell** on the floating card to show the formula, intermediate results and links to its inputs. When a source row came from a screenshot, **View Screenshot Source** opens that row and its image in Scratch. Click the chevron again to return to the number.


---
title: "Selection History"
description: "Compare earlier cell entries and recover a range without rolling back the sheet."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/history
---

# Selection History

**Select the cells you want to recover and choose Show Selection History from the sheet menu or the command palette.**

## Compare a revision

Pick a revision to see the selected cells that differ from the current sheet. **Before** shows the entries and formatting just before that edit. **Now** shows what is in the grid. Changed entries or formats are emphasised. Formula cells show the expression that will be restored. Hover over the revision time for the exact date and time.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/history-revision-light.webp" alt="Selection History compares the previous and current venue and catering amounts." width="944" height="496" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/history-revision-dark.webp" alt="Selection History compares the previous and current venue and catering amounts." width="944" height="496" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Restore just the range

Enter `10` in A1 and `=A1*2` in B1. Change A1 to `15`, then select A1:B1 and open **Show Selection History**. Choose the revision before the last edit and click **Restore A1:B1**. A1 returns to `10` and B1 recalculates to `20`.

Scratch restores entries and formatting inside the selected range. Cells outside it keep their current entries. Formulas recalculate using the current sheet, including any references outside the range. Press ⌘Z to reverse the restore in one step.

History starts with edits made after installing this build and stays in the workbook on your Mac across launches. Scratch keeps up to 100 recent grid edits per sheet. Large edits can reduce how many older revisions are kept.


---
title: "Record and Replay"
description: "Save a sequence of grid commands and run it on another range."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/replay
---

# Record and Replay

**Open the command palette and choose Start Recording.** Run up to 12 steps, then choose **Save Recording**, type a name and press Return.

Scratch can record **Fill Down**, **Fill Right**, **Clear Cell Contents** and cell formatting commands. You can use their shortcuts, the Format menu or the command palette. The commands take effect as you record them. To discard the recording, choose **Cancel Recording**. Use Undo in the grid to reverse an edit you made while recording.

## Try it on another range

1. Select a column of cells with a formula in the first row. Record **Fill Down**, **Format as AUD** and **Add Decimal Place**.
2. Save the recording as **AUD totals**. Select a different range with its own formula in the first row.
3. In the command palette, choose **Replay AUD totals**. Scratch highlights the cells it would change and shows their resulting text.
4. Press Return to apply the replay as one edit, or Escape to discard the preview. Press ⌘Z to undo the applied replay.

Each step uses the new selection’s contents and formatting. Relative references shift as they do with ordinary Fill Down and Fill Right. Scratch saves named replays on this Mac. Use **Remove Saved Replay** in the command palette to remove one.

<source src="/docs/replay-demo-light.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

<video class="scratch-dark" controls muted loop playsinline preload="none" aria-label="Record fill and formatting commands, then preview the changes on the Sunday receipts." poster="/docs/replay-preview-dark.webp" width="1240" height="780">

---
title: "Keyboard Shortcuts"
description: "Choose your own shortcuts for Notes, the command palette and capture."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/shortcuts
---

# Keyboard Shortcuts

**Click the ⋯ button in Scratch and open Keyboard Shortcuts.** Choose a **Change** command and press the combination you want. Press Escape to cancel, or choose **Reset** in the menu to restore a default.

| Action | Default | Where it works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Scratch | ⌥ Space | From any app |
| Capture Clipboard | ⌥⇧ Space | From any app |
| Show or Hide Notes | ⌘J | In Scratch |
| Command Palette | ⇧⌘P | In Scratch |
| Focus Notes or Grid | ⌥⌘J | In Scratch |
| Send to Obsidian | ⇧⌘J | In Scratch |
| Find a Sheet | ⌘K | In Scratch |
| Next or Previous Sheet | ⌃Tab or ⌃⇧Tab | In Scratch |
| Nudge Cell Up or Down | ⌃⌥↑ or ⌃⌥↓ | On the grid |

If another app intercepts a shortcut, click **Notes** or choose **Command Palette** from the ⋯ menu while you change the binding. For example, try ⌃⌥N for Notes and ⌃⌥P for the palette if those combinations are available on your Mac. Scratch flags conflicts with its own shortcuts.

Open the command palette and type **Freeze**, **Sort Rows**, **Filter Rows** or **Clear Row Filter**. Tab moves through the sort and filter controls. In Sort, adjust **Rows to move** when needed, choose an order, and click **Apply Sort**. In Filter, type to update the results and press Return to keep them. Press Escape to cancel the preview. [Grid and shortcuts](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#freeze-rows-and-columns).

Use **Dock Notes Left**, **Dock Notes Right**, **Dock Notes Top**, **Dock Notes Bottom** or **Detach Notes** in the command palette to arrange the workspace from the keyboard. ⌥⌘J also switches focus between the floating windows. [Move or detach panes](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#move-or-detach-panes).

Choose **Tables** in the command palette to find a table or its actions. **Create Table from Selection** goes straight to naming. With a cell in a named table selected, **Sort Rows** and **Filter Rows** use that table. [Named tables](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#named-tables).

Use **Hide Selected Rows**, **Hide Selected Columns**, **Show All Rows**, **Show All Columns** or **Fit Row Height** in the command palette. Option-drag a row or column header to move it. [Move, hide or resize rows and columns](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#move-hide-or-resize-rows-and-columns).

Find **New Workbook**, **Open Workbook**, **Open Default Workbook**, **Archive Current Sheet**, **Import Excel Values** and TSV export in the command palette. [Workbooks and sheet archive](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#workbooks-and-sheet-archive).

## Switch sheets

Press ⌘K or choose **Switch Sheet** in the command palette. The last sheets you visited in this workbook appear first, with the cell you left selected on each. Press Return to reopen the first result, or type part of a sheet name. Use the arrows to highlight a result and Escape to return to your current sheet.

Press ⌃Tab to move forward in workbook order or ⌃⇧Tab to move backward. Both wrap around and skip archived sheets. ⌘1 through ⌘9 still jump to sheets in workbook order. Click the sheet title to find actions such as Rename and Export.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/sheet-switcher-light.webp" alt="The sheet switcher lists Coast trip with its last selected cell and marks November budget as the current sheet." width="1120" height="690" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/sheet-switcher-dark.webp" alt="The sheet switcher lists Coast trip with its last selected cell and marks November budget as the current sheet." width="1120" height="690" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

## Nudge a number or date

Select a cell on the grid and press ⌃⌥↑ or ⌃⌥↓. A number moves by one, a date by one day and a percentage by one percentage point. Hold Shift for ten, one week or ten percentage points.

Dependent formulas update as you hold the key. Release it and press ⌘Z to undo the full adjustment. Select a formula’s input cell to adjust the result. **Nudge Cell Up** and **Nudge Cell Down** are also in the command palette.

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/cell-nudge-light.webp" alt="The command palette shows Nudge Cell Up and Nudge Cell Down with their keyboard shortcuts." width="547" height="327" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/cell-nudge-dark.webp" alt="The command palette shows Nudge Cell Up and Nudge Cell Down with their keyboard shortcuts." width="547" height="327" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>

<figure class="scratch-media">
<img class="scratch-light" src="/docs/palette-shortcuts-light.webp" alt="The command palette shows formatting actions with their keyboard shortcuts." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<img class="scratch-dark" src="/docs/palette-shortcuts-dark.webp" alt="The command palette shows formatting actions with their keyboard shortcuts." width="1280" height="840" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</figure>


---
title: "A cleaner workspace (2026-11-13)"
description: "A lighter grid, a roomier palette, and controls that line up across Scratch."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/changelog/2026-11-13-workspace-polish
---

# A cleaner workspace (2026-11-13)

**The grid, formula bar and Notes use aligned controls and consistent insets.** The palette fits its results and highlights matching text. Choose **Natural**, **Snappy** or **Off** under **Animation Style**. Use **Follow System Accent** to match macOS.

**Preview a paste without shifting the grid.** The bar shows the paste modes and flags cells you’ll replace. Capture review has previous and next controls, a **Mark Correct** button and a progress bar beside the source.

**Trace a formula to the cell behind an error.** The microscope shows the chain and a jump to the source. The expanded formula bar pairs each reference colour with the cells it covers. Selection History highlights changes to entries and formats.

**Notes keeps the Markdown and shows a quieter view while you edit.** Lists show bullets and checkboxes. Live tables use a text header when one is present, and numeric values line up at the right. Hover over Send to see what will go to Obsidian. A confirmed send leaves a receipt and a link.

**Undo a sheet deletion from the footer.** Click **Undo** or press ⌘Z after deleting a sheet. Use **Restore Deleted Sheet** to bring it back later.

[Getting started](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/getting-started.md) · [Capture and paste](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/capture.md) · [Formula Microscope](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/formula-microscope.md) · [Notes and Obsidian](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian.md)

title: "See where your tables are (2026-11-13)"

# See where your tables are (2026-11-13)

**Start a named table from a selection or a filled cell.** Scratch previews the range and tells you which row becomes the header. After you name it, the tinted header and outline show where the table sits in the sheet.

Docked Notes opens and closes from the divider. Reopen it to continue reading or editing where you left off. Nearby jumps scroll into view, and distant jumps use a short fade. You can choose the pace under **Animation Style** or use macOS Reduce Motion.

To bring edits back from Obsidian, edit the note in `Scratch/Editable Tables` and run **Sync Editable Table with Obsidian** in Scratch. Use `Scratch/Sheets` for dated snapshots.

[Named tables](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#named-tables) · [Notes and Obsidian](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian.md#edit-a-table-in-both-scratch-and-obsidian)

# Find a sheet or cycle straight to it (2026-11-13)

**Press ⌃Tab to move to the next sheet or ⌃⇧Tab to go back.** Scratch wraps around the workbook and skips archived sheets. Each sheet keeps its selection and scroll position.

# Notes on every edge (2026-11-13)

**Drag Notes to the top, bottom, left or right edge, or drag it out into its own window.** Scratch remembers a separate size for each edge and keeps your grid selection, Notes caret and scroll position as you move it. Drag the dotted divider to resize. Double-click it to reset.

Sort now shows **Rows to move**. To sort amounts in rows 2 through 4 and keep a total on row 5, enter `2:4`. When a sort would break up a formula range, the preview names the formula cell and its range.

**Annotate Selection** puts the caret in the editor when it opens. Editable Obsidian notes now give the Markdown table its own block. Sync an older editable note again to update it in place.

[Move or detach panes](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#move-or-detach-panes) · [Sort rows](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#sort-rows) · [Notes and Obsidian](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian.md)

# Find your way back and see formula arguments (2026-11-13)

# Copy a range as Markdown, a total or an image (2026-11-13)

**Export groups its actions by selection, table, sheet and workbook.** The Selection heading shows the current range. When the active cell is in a named table, the Table heading shows its name.

# Sort and filter at the column (2026-11-13)

# Borders and table styling (2026-11-13)

# "Workbooks and formulas (2026-11-12)" (2026-11-12)

**Move, hide and resize at the grid edge.** Option-drag a row or column header to move it. Right-click a header to hide it. Drag the bottom of a row header to set its height. [Grid controls](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#move-hide-or-resize-rows-and-columns).

**Use formulas across sheets.** Reference a cell or range on another sheet, calculate with saved named ranges, or use XLOOKUP to find a matching value. There are new date and text functions too. [Work across sheets](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#work-across-sheets).

**Keep separate workbooks and move data between apps.** Open a local workbook, archive a sheet, or exchange TSV and Excel values. Each sheet now fits 2,000 rows and 96 columns. [Workbooks and file formats](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#workbooks-and-sheet-archive).

# Named tables (2026-11-12)

# Scratch local preview (2026-11-12)

**Scratch opens over the app you’re in with ⌥ Space.** Type in the grid, complete a formula with Tab and use the command palette to find actions.

Capture clipboard amounts and screenshots in a new sheet. Keep notes beside the numbers and insert live values, tables or a bar chart. Send the table and notes to an Obsidian daily note or save a dated sheet note.

A/B scenarios were removed in a later update. [Read the removal note](/changelog/2026-11-12-remove-scenarios).

The app is available as a local build from an existing source checkout. The [getting started guide](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/getting-started.md) walks through the first calculation.

# See what to fix beside a cell (2026-11-12)

**Input checks mark the cells that need attention.** Select a flagged cell to see what to fix. Division by zero and other formula errors get the same treatment automatically. [Check inputs as you edit](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#check-inputs-as-you-edit).


---
title: "Freeze panes, sort and filter (2026-11-12)"
description: "Keep labels visible, sort complete rows and narrow a sheet by what you see in a column."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/changelog/2026-11-12-freeze-sort-filter
---

# Freeze panes, sort and filter (2026-11-12)

**Keep labels in view as you scroll.** Freeze the rows above and columns to the left of your selection. Drag either divider’s blue grip to move the boundary. Scratch remembers each sheet’s setting. [Freeze panes](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#freeze-rows-and-columns).

**Sort rows together.** Pick a column and review the row bounds before applying. Formulas, linked notes and annotations follow their source cells. Undo restores the original order. [Sort rows](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#sort-rows).

**Filter by what you see.** Enter part of a value and move through the matching rows with the keyboard. Click the match count in the footer to clear the filter. CSV exports and Obsidian sync keep the hidden rows. [Filter rows](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#filter-rows).

title: "Editable Obsidian tables (2026-11-12)"
description: "Edit cells in Scratch and Obsidian, then merge the changes on demand."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/changelog/2026-11-12-editable-obsidian-tables
---

# Editable Obsidian tables (2026-11-12)

**Run Sync Editable Table with Obsidian to make an editable copy of a Scratch sheet in your vault.**

Open the copy from Scratch, edit in either app, and sync again. Edits to different cells merge. If the same cell changes to different values in both apps, Scratch shows the address so you can resolve it. Changes pulled into Scratch can be undone in one step.

The Power Tables community plugin can edit and recalculate compatible formulas. [Read the editable table guide](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian.md#edit-a-table-in-both-scratch-and-obsidian).

title: "Drag across more of the grid (2026-11-12)"

# Drag across more of the grid (2026-11-12)

**Hold a drag at the grid edge to keep scrolling.** The range follows the pointer as rows or columns come into view. Move back inside the grid to pause scrolling, or release to finish.

This works for ordinary and Shift selection, the fill handle and formula references. [Grid and shortcuts](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#move-and-select).


---
title: "Drag results and expand formulas (2026-11-12)"
description: "Place calculations, link Notes to cells, and edit long formulas in a larger bar."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/changelog/2026-11-12-drag-and-expand
---

# Drag results and expand formulas (2026-11-12)

**Drag Sum or Avg from the footer into an empty cell.** Scratch previews the formula before you drop it. Hold Option to insert the current value. The command palette can place either result by address. [Grid guide](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#calculate-and-copy).

**Drag between the grid and Notes.** Option-drag a selected range into Notes for a live table. Add Shift for a chart or Command for a link. Option-drag selected note text to the grid to annotate a cell or range. [Notes guide](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian.md#put-a-live-result-in-a-note).

**Expand the formula bar with ⌥⌘E or the chevron.** Long expressions wrap. Underlined references match their grid outlines, and the current argument and matching parentheses highlight as you move the caret. Collapse the bar to keep editing at the same position. [Formula editing](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#calculate-and-copy).


---
title: "Convert currency from the palette (2026-11-12)"
description: "Copy a conversion with a dated ECB reference rate."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/changelog/2026-11-12-currency-conversion
---

# Convert currency from the palette (2026-11-12)

**Type `100 AUD to USD` in the command palette.** Fetch the ECB rates, then copy the converted number. Scratch shows the exchange rate and its date, and keeps the last fetched rates for offline use. [Convert currency](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/grid.md#convert-currency).


---
title: "Annotate cells and ranges (2026-11-12)"
description: "Leave a note on a specific part of the grid and jump back to it later."
canonical_url: https://scratch.itsryan.me/changelog/2026-11-12-cell-annotations
---

# Annotate cells and ranges (2026-11-12)

**Choose Annotate Selection to leave a note on a cell or range.** Click the marker to reopen it, or use **Find Annotations** to jump to it from the command palette. [Annotate a cell or range](https://scratch.itsryan.me/docs/notes-and-obsidian.md#annotate-a-cell-or-range).
